title: SIEM forwarder reliability and customer requirements spec
content:
Purpose:
This working doc captures requirements and a pragmatic connector spec focused on forwarder reliability (replay, at-least-once vs at-most-once semantics), customer onboarding checklist, and operational behavior across Splunk (HEC), Datadog (Events API / Logs intake), and Microsoft Sentinel (Azure Event Hubs / CEF). It also calls out RBAC v2 constraints and evidence-automation hooks for compliance customers.

Audience:
- Platform engineering and security teams building SIEM exporters
- Solutions engineers onboarding customers for SIEM exports
- SRE/observability owners responsible for exporter SLAs

Status and context:
- Draft for review with solutions-eng and product-hosted-api teams.
- Intention: consolidate common requirements we get from enterprise customers (replay guarantees, evidence artifacts, retention controls) into a single spec that connector engineers can implement.

Goals:
- Define minimal guarantees for delivery (ACK model, retries, replay window).
- Provide sample event payloads for three target sinks (Splunk HEC, Datadog Logs/Events, Sentinel).
- Specify metadata mappings to audit log schema and evidence automation fields.
- Create an onboarding checklist customers must satisfy before enabling export (networking, auth, RBAC).
- Surface edge cases (backpressure, partial failures) and recommended operator behavior.

Assumptions:
- Exports originate from the Redwood control plane or from Private/VPC forwarder (configurable).
- Customers may require PII redaction prior to export — this doc assumes field-redaction happens server-side if requested; connector still supports an allowlist mapping.
- We support both JSON and CEF/plain-text transports depending on sink.

Customer onboarding checklist (minimum):
- Network: provide destination endpoint(s), TLS cert details, and IP allowlist entry for Redwood egress IPs or peering info for Private deployments.
- Auth: HEC token (Splunk), API key (Datadog), SAS or Managed Identity + Event Hub namespace details (Sentinel).
- Retention/Retention Controls: desired retention window for evidence copies (if evidence export enabled), and legal hold flags.
- RBAC: designate an admin user to configure export (see RBAC v2 section) and a list of read-only reviewers.
- Sampling: specify whether the customer wants full audit export, rate-limited export, or sample sets (default: full).
- Test window: agree on a 48-hour test window with sample traffic for validation and mapping checks.

Delivery semantics (recommended):
- Default mode: at-least-once delivery with idempotency keys when sink supports it. Justification: audit data is compliance-sensitive; we prefer duplicates over drop.
- Idempotency: add a deterministic event_id for every exported record (UUIDv4 or sha256(document)) and include event_seq for ordering within a session if available.
- Acknowledgement model: connector tracks per-batch ACKs from sink and retries until success or connector-configured retry budget expires.
- Replay: persistent export queue (on disk + WAL for stateful forwarders) supporting replay of up to N days (configurable per-customer). Default replay window: 7 days.
- Backpressure: if sink reports rate-limit (429) or TCP backpressure, connector should switch into exponential backoff with jitter and enter a safe-disk-queue mode; alert SRE after 5 minutes of sustained backpressure.
- Dead-letter: on persistent schema or auth errors, route to DLQ and surface actionable error to customer and Redwood SRE. DLQ retention default: 30 days.

Connector transport and auth per-sink:
- Splunk (HEC): HTTPS POST to /services/collector/event/1.0 with HEC token header. Support batching and compressed payloads. Provide examples for single-event and batch.
- Datadog: HTTP API /v1/input with API key in query param or header (document both). Support logs ingestion or events API depending on customer choice. Use Datadog bulk endpoints where possible.
- Sentinel: push to Azure Event Hubs or use Sentinel CEF connector depending on customer. For Event Hubs, support SAS and MSI auth. When CEF is required, export as syslog over TLS to customer's CEF collector.

Field mapping and audit log schema (source -> sink suggested mapping):
- Common Redwood audit fields (recommended canonical schema):
  - event_id: string (uuid)
  - timestamp: ISO8601 string (utc)
  - actor: { id, type, email } (flattened actor_id, actor_type, actor_email)
  - action: string (e.g., model.invoke, config.update)
  - resource: { id, type, name } (flattened resource_id, resource_type, resource_name)
  - outcome: success|failure|partial
  - client_ip: ip
  - user_agent: string
  - request_id: string (Redwood request id)
  - token_usage: tokens_in, tokens_out (optional numeric fields)
  - model_version: string
  - redaction_flags: list (redacted_fields)

Mapping notes:
- Splunk: send event as the top-level JSON object. Use host/source/sourcetype fields: sourcetype=redwood:audit, source=redwood:export, host=<customer-id>. Include event_id as splunk_event_id and _time mapped from timestamp.
- Datadog: map timestamp->date, event_id->dd.event_id attribute, and include a top-level "redwood" object with canonical fields to avoid collisions.
- Sentinel: when using CEF, map critical fields into CEF extension keys (rt, suid for session id, request id) and include full JSON as part of extension or additional data.

Sample events (high level examples):
- Splunk HEC single event (JSON):
  {
    "time": "2026-02-14T19:22:05Z",
    "host": "cust-42",
    "sourcetype": "redwood:audit",
    "event": {
      "event_id": "b12a7f6e-...",
      "actor_id": "user-87",
      "action": "model.invoke",
      "resource_id": "model-abc:v2",
      "outcome": "success",
      "request_id": "req-999",
      "tokens_in": 18
    }
  }

- Datadog logs bulk (ndjson): each line is JSON with timestamp and attributes; include ddsource=redwood, service=redwood-audit.

- Sentinel (Event Hub JSON): same canonical JSON object, include metadata.headers.redwood-version and headers.exporter-region.

Evidence automation hooks (compliance customers):
- Evidence artifact: when a request triggers a compliance-evidence flag, export an evidence object with link to object store (signed URL) plus manifest fields: evidence_id, related_event_id, retention_ttl, legal_hold_flag.
- Evidence TTL: customer config option; default 90 days unless legal_hold set. Evidence objects are stored encrypted (KMS) and the connector will export only metadata to SIEM (link+hash).
- Correlation: include evidence_id in both audit event and in the SIEM export so downstream EDR/SIEM workflows can attach artifacts.

RBAC v2 considerations (who can do what):
- Only users with security.admin or exporter.admin roles can create or modify SIEM export connectors.
- Read-only roles (security.viewer) can view exports and status but cannot rotate keys or change endpoints.
- Connector credentials stored in customer secrets vault and decrypted only at forwarder runtime. Audit all credential operations to audit log.

Operational runbook (SRE actions):
- Metrics to export from connector: export_success_count, export_failure_count, avg_export_latency_ms, current_queue_depth, dlq_rate, last_success_timestamp, last_failure_reason.
- Alerts:
  - P1: sustained export failures >5m and queue_depth growing for >10m => page SRE and SE.
  - P2: authentication failures >3 in 5m => notify customer onboarding lead.
  - P3: evidence export size > configured limit => warn and throttle.
- Run commands for troubleshooting:
  - tail connector logs with request_id filter.
  - replay from WAL for a given time window: connector replay --from 2026-02-12T00:00Z --to 2026-02-12T03:00Z --dry-run
  - force rotate HEC token or regenerate SAS and verify connectivity.

Edge cases and recommendations:
- Partial batch success: prefer splitting large batches on 413/invalid-payload and retry smaller batches.
- Schema drifts: when new fields appear, connector should forward unknowns verbatim under "extra" map to avoid data loss and mark mapping version in metadata.
- Duplicate suppression: rely on event_id idempotency where sink supports it; otherwise, accept duplicates and provide dedupe utilities in customer's SIEM query templates.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Determine default disk quota for on-disk queues per customer and pricing implications. (TODO: pricing and quota PRD)
- Should we support encrypted-at-rest evidence payloads streaming directly to customer-managed S3/Azure blob instead of storing in Redwood object store? Need privacy/legal input. (action: loop in legal)
- Confirm Datadog rate limits per plan and whether we should throttle per-customer rather than global. (owner: Priya)
- Provide sample Sentinel CEF mapping for the 10 most common Redwood audit actions. (owner: Asha)

Appendix: quick diagnostic checklist for solutions engineers:
- Verify network: curl to HEC endpoint with provided token (use test payload).
- Verify mapping: request sample event set from Redwood staging for mapping validation.
- Validate retention: check that evidence TTL and legal_hold flags are correctly configured before enabling live export.
- Document expected volume: estimate events per-minute and peak burst; use this to size connector queue and retry budget.

Known related artifacts and tickets:
- SEC-3421 (export reliability backlog)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/siem-connectors/pull/78 (initial replay implementation)

Notes to self / rough ideas (scratch):
- Consider a lightweight verification API that customers can hit to validate mapping and auth without generating real audit events (replay-mode test events).
- Think about adding a small client-side SDK for B2B customers to annotate evidence IDs at request time so correlation is deterministic.

Last reviewed by: Marcus Liu (security), Priya Nair (solutions-eng)

-- end of doc --
